imp.generic: On the seventh night, I noticed the candle was dripping.
imp.author: It was upon the seventh night of my vigil that the candle first began to weep.

imp.generic: You probably think I was crazy.
imp.author: Was it madness? You will say it was madness. But tell me, then, you who have never sat alone with the dead hours pressing upon your skull like wet linen.

imp.generic: The wax pooled into the shape of a small hand.
imp.author: Why the wax should pool upon the floor in the very shape of a hand. A small hand. A child's hand.

imp.generic: The portrait seemed to change a little each day.
imp.author: First with curiosity, then with a creeping and intolerable horror, I observed that the portrait was changing. Not the face! It was the eyes.

imp.generic: I heard a strange breathing sound and it matched my own breathing.
imp.author: When I gasped, it gasped. When I stilled myself in terror, it too grew still, and I understood, with a clarity that scalded me, that the breathing was matching itself to my own.

imp.generic: After I bricked up the wall, I heard tapping behind it.
imp.author: The wall was scarcely dry when the tapping began. A delicate sound, the merest articulation of knuckle upon stone, patient, rhythmic, unmistakably a summons.

imp.generic: A voice on the other side asked me to let it out.
imp.author: I felt the answering pressure of a cheek upon the other side, warm through the stone, and heard the murmur say, so very gently: Let me out. Let me out. You know me.

imp.generic: The old clock had thirteen hours on its face.
imp.author: Grief sharpens the eye to monstrous particulars, and on the night of the interment I saw it plainly, a thirteenth numeral, struck in tarnished silver where no numeral has any right to dwell.

imp.generic: I won't describe what I found in the alcove.
imp.author: Reader, I will not tell you what crouched within that alcove. I will say only that it wore my brother's coat, and that it had been waiting, patiently, oh so patiently.

imp.generic: I realized the room wasn't really safe; the marsh was going to swallow me.
imp.author: I had not taken shelter in a house at all, but had crept, fevered and unknowing, into the open and waiting jaws of the marsh itself, which now drew breath to swallow me down.
